findings.issue_text: [BUG] UpgradeTest references a FeatureSpec class and a getFeatureSpec()/setFeatureSpec() accessor on the v2alpha1 KeycloakSpec that do not exist anywhere in this diff or in the upstream v2alpha1 CRD (which only has UnsupportedSpec), so the test does not compile. The operator integration test module fails to build with 'cannot find symbol: class FeatureSpec' and 'cannot find symbol: method getFeatureSpec()', breaking CI for the whole PR.

[BUG] UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata call picocli.exit(...) but the diff adds no field, import, or accessor named 'picocli' to AbstractUpdatesCommand, so the symbol is unresolved. The quarkus runtime module fails to compile ('cannot find symbol: variable picocli') unless an unshown external change supplies this member; if AbstractUpdatesCommand lacks it, the feature-disabled path never works at all.

[ADVISORY] If picocli.exit(int) merely records the exit code rather than throwing (as keycloak's AbstractCommand exit helpers do), the early-return run() path leaves the command completing 'normally' and the FEATURE_DISABLED code (4) may be overwritten by the default success path. Scripts and the operator reading the documented exit code 4 to detect 'feature disabled' (docs table row m|4) instead observe exit code 0, silently misclassifying a blocked upgrade as a successful one.

[ADVISORY] The operator documentation asserts the Operator 'will fail' when rolling-updates is not enabled, but no operator-side enforcement (reconciler check or CRD validation) exists anywhere in this diff. Operators following the doc discover the Operator silently proceeds with Recreate behavior (or crashes elsewhere) instead of the documented failure, eroding trust in the guide; the caution is only actionable once enforcement code ships.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code 4, so the exit-code contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc row 'm|4' is unverified. A regression that prints the message but exits 0 (e.g. someone drops the picocli.exit call) passes the test while operator/scripts consuming exit code 4 silently treat a feature-disabled run as success; also the newly introduced FEATURE_DISABLED constant has no test asserting its value anywhere in the diff.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3, breaking any existing automation that checks exit code 4 for 'recreate required'. Scripts (and any operator-side code predating this diff) that branch on exit code 4 as 'rolling upgrade not possible' now interpret it as the new feature-disabled signal, and exit code 3 flows through code paths that previously never produced it; the diff updates the docs table but contains no changelog note and testWrongVersions asserts only the error text, never the exit code, so the new mapping of incompatible-check to 3 is completely unverified.

[ADVISORY] The diff modifies the operator test only to enable the new feature, but no test anywhere verifies the documented behavior that the Keycloak Operator fails when the rolling-updates feature is disabled (advanced-configuration.adoc CAUTION: 'Otherwise the {project_name} Operator will fail'). The feature-disabled operator path (the primary new acceptance criterion for the operator) has zero coverage — a regression where the operator proceeds without the feature enabled would not be caught, and the test suite never even exercises a Keycloak CR without FeatureSpec.setEnabledFeatures.

[ADVISORY] The preview feature is enabled only in the custom test image Dockerfile, with no gating-flag propagation audit for other operator test images or the production operator image path touched in this diff. Any operator integration test not built from Dockerfile-custom-image (or a future production image build) will run against Keycloak without rolling-updates enabled and hit the 'Operator will fail' path from the docs caution, making the upgrade-strategy tests silently dependent on which image the CI pipeline happens to build.

[BUG] Changing RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 silently repurposes exit code 4 (previously 'recreate upgrade required') to mean 'feature disabled', breaking any existing automation or operator logic that interprets exit code 4 as 'must recreate'. Downstream scripts/CI that branch on exit code 4 to trigger a shutdown-and-recreate upgrade now receive code 4 when the feature is merely disabled — or code 3, a value they have never seen — and either take no action or fail, while no deprecation path or release-note-worthy migration is present in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The documentation claims 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' when rolling-updates is not enabled, but this diff contains no operator-side code that checks or enforces the feature flag — the only enforcement added is in the two kc CLI commands. Operators reading this guide enable the flag expecting operator behavior change; if the operator-side failure is delivered by a companion PR not shown here, the docs and code ship out of sync, and if it does not exist the documented failure mode is unimplemented — either way the stated invariant is not enforced by this diff.

[ADVISORY] The feature gate is duplicated verbatim in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run rather than enforced once in the shared parent AbstractUpdatesCommand, so a future third subcommand added under update-compatibility ships without the gate. The next maintainer adding a subcommand inherits a silent enforcement gap — the docs' blanket claim 'Otherwise, the commands will fail' becomes false for the new command; passing the deletion test, hoisting the check into AbstractUpdatesCommand deletes both duplicated blocks.

[ADVISORY] The custom operator test image now unconditionally bakes --features=rolling-updates into the build, permanently enabling the preview feature for all operator integration tests regardless of the scenario under test. The operator test suite can no longer exercise the default (feature-disabled) deployment path that real users hit per the new CAUTION box, and any future test asserting feature-off behavior will need to fight this image-level override.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3, re-purposing exit code 4 as FEATURE_DISABLED with no version bump or compatibility note for existing consumers of the CLI's process contract. Any external automation, CI pipeline, or operator-side wrapper written against the previously shipped behavior (recreate-required == 4) now reads exit 3 for recreate and exit 4 for 'feature disabled', so a recreate-required result is misclassified or the disabled error is misread as 'recreate required'; consumers get the wrong upgrade decision without any error being raised.

[ADVISORY] The documentation claims 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' when rolling-updates is disabled, but the diff contains no operator-side code that enforces this — the only operator changes are the Dockerfile build flag and the integration test enabling the feature. Operators running a Keycloak CR with spec.update.strategy set but the feature not enabled follow documented-but-unimplemented behavior: if the enforcement lives elsewhere the doc is unverifiable from this change, and if it doesn't exist the operator proceeds into a rolling-update path the server-side framework (gated CLI commands) considers disabled, leaving users in an undocumented middle state.

[ADVISORY] The custom test image bakes --features=rolling-updates into the container build, so every operator integration test running against this image executes with the feature force-enabled and never exercises the disabled-path behavior the docs claim the operator exhibits. The operator test suite is a stand-in guard that can go green while the feature-disabled path (operator failure mode) is red in production: a regression that breaks the operator when rolling-updates is off is invisible to this suite because the fixture image silently enables it.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3, breaking the externally documented exit-code contract of the update-compatibility command. Any existing consumer of `kc.sh update-compatibility` (operator automation, CI scripts, docs-published guidance) that branches on exit code 4 == 'recreate required' now misinterprets exit 4 as 'feature disabled' (a different condition), causing scripts to attempt or skip rolling upgrades based on the wrong verdict.

[ADVISORY] The new CAUTION states the Keycloak Operator will fail without the feature enabled, but this diff contains no operator reconciliation code that actually enforces or reports that failure. Operators reading the guide will expect a clear failure signal when rolling-updates is disabled with update.strategy set; if the enforcing logic was silently dropped or lives elsewhere, they get an undocumented behavior (pod build failures from the CLI exit code FEATURE_DISABLED=4 surfacing as opaque pod crashes) instead of a stated operator error, and the doc promise cannot be verified against this change set.

[ADVISORY] FEATURE_DISABLED is assigned exit code 4, silently reusing the value that previously meant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE, so any existing consumer checking `== 4` to decide 'recreate upgrade required' now receives that verdict when the feature is disabled. Operators or scripts that branched on exit code 4 as 'must recreate' before this change will take the recreate path (or skip an upgrade check entirely) when the real condition is 'feature flag off' — a wrong automated decision during a production upgrade; only in-diff docs were updated, out-of-tree consumers of the CLI contract get no signal.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4) that UpdateCompatibilityCheck/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata now return via picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED). A regression that prints the same message but returns exit code 0 or 1 passes this test; the operator, which branches on the exit code per the documented outcome table (row 4 = feature disabled), silently misclassifies the result.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 (a breaking change to the CLI's machine-consumable contract) yet no test in this diff asserts the exit code of the recreate/incompatible path — testWrongVersions (UpdateCommandDistTest lines ~96-105) asserts only the '[Versions] Rolling Upgrade is not available' message and never calls result.exitCode(). Any consumer (e.g. the Operator or user scripts) coded against exit code 4 for 'recreate required' now receives 3 with no test failing if the value drifts again or is accidentally reverted; the change to the contract is entirely unverified.

[ADVISORY] testMissingOptionOnSave was updated to add ENABLE_FEATURE but still asserts assertNoMessage("Missing required argument"), a negative existence assertion that passes regardless of whether the metadata command actually validates its required options, while testMissingOptionOnCheck asserts the positive error — the save path's option validation remains verified only by absence. If metadata-side required-argument validation regresses (either stops enforcing the option or changes the message wording), this test still passes, giving false confidence that the save command's input validation is covered.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from the already-shipped 4 to 3 in the same release that repurposes 4 to mean FEATURE_DISABLED, so existing automation that was built against the documented exit code 4 (recreate required) now misclassifies every recreate-required result. An operator's wrapper script or CI pipeline that ran a previously released `kc.sh update-compatibility check` and branches on exit code 4 ('recreate upgrade required') will, after this change, treat a recreate-required result (now exit 3) as an unexpected failure, and treat a feature-disabled result (exit 4) as 'recreate required' — the deployment decision is silently inverted; rolling-back the server binary also breaks new scripts written against the new codes, so neither deploy direction coexists cleanly.

[ADVISORY] The feature gate is enforced only at command runtime via Profile.isFeatureEnabled, so the exit-code semantic change and the feature gate land in one step with no expand/contract transition for consumers of the old exit codes. Operators upgrading a Keycloak instance that previously executed update-compatibility without the flag now get exit 4 with a different meaning plus a hard failure of the command they relied on, forcing a config change (enable rolling-updates) and script rewrite simultaneously during a single upgrade window.

[ADVISORY] FEATURE_DISABLED reuses exit code 4, the value previously published as RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE, so existing automation that branches on exit code 4 (per the pre-change docs contract '4 = Rolling Upgrade is not possible, deployment must be shut down') now silently interprets a feature-disabled hard failure as a recreate-required verdict and proceeds to shut down the deployment for the wrong reason. Operators with scripts parsing `kc.sh update-compatibility check` exit codes written against the old contract get exit 4 both for 'recreate required' and for 'feature disabled'; the script takes the recreate path (shutdown) when the real problem is a misconfiguration, and the distinction is only recoverable by parsing stderr text.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled path calls printFeatureDisabled() (an error print) followed by picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED), but the run() contract elsewhere in this class distinguishes user-facing outcomes via CompatibilityResult exit codes and validated messages; a caller that invokes run() programmatically rather than via the CLI launcher receives no exception and no result object, only a side-effect print and an exit-code side channel, so the failure is invisible to any in-process caller. Any embedding of the update-compatibility check (e.g. an operator or provisioning tool invoking the command in-process) sees run() return normally and cannot distinguish the disabled-feature refusal from success without inspecting the process exit code, which only exists in the forked-CLI case.
